Q: How do I determine the state of a VBA workbook before attemting to close it (Excel 2007)? A:

Thanks for this, Tim. It appears to work. It boils down to the fact that you have been able to trap the <automation error> against wb.Name whereas I wasn't against wb on its own. Maybe it is something to do with the type. Here is a stripped down piece of code to show how it works with wb.Name

Const scPathFile as String = "C:\Dir\abc.xlsx"

dim s as string

dim wb as workbook

set wb = workbooks.Open(scPathFile)

wb.Close

On Error Resume Next

s = wb.name

wb.Close

s takes the value "". Without On Error Resume Next it throws an automation error when the workbook is not fully formed.

Q: GuzzleHttp give me 500 error A:

http://docs.guzzlephp.org/en/latest/request-options.html#jso

Summary:

The json option is used to easily upload JSON encoded data as the body of a request. A Content-Type header of application/json will be added if no Content-Type header is already present on the message.

Here's an example on how to set up the header on request:

$client->request('POST', $url, [
    'headers' => [
        'Accept'     => 'application/json',
    ],
    'body' = $body
]);

Q: What is the maximum file path allowed in Android A:

AOSP ≥ 14 utilises EXT4 for its root filesystem (like /data/media/0/; basically, all except mounted ones, for which I believe that solely exFAT is a possible user-facing alternative). EXT4 has no filesystem-defined maximum path length. [1]

However, userspace APIs (that don't contribute to exhaustion of the available file descriptors) are limited by what the Linux kernel defines in PATH_MAX, usually 4096 characters. [2] Unfortunately, programmatically verifying (and, by extension, relying upon) it isn't recommended. [3]

Q: Localization/Internationalization: If I import a fruits list once with English and 2nd time with Chinese locale, what should be displayed by website? A:

The system must display the raw data exactly as imported.

  • Scenario 1 (English Data, Chinese UI): Shows English. The locale changes the interface (labels/buttons), not the payload.

  • Scenario 2 (Chinese Data, English UI): Shows Chinese. The system shouldn't auto-translate user content; that violates data integrity.

Logic: Localization = UI translation. Content = Immutable user input. Mixing them creates a system conflict where the software assumes authority over the user's data, which is a design flaw.

Q: Intelephense in VS Code doesn't recognize a php variable from included file A:

Intelephense does static analysis — it doesn't actually execute the include, so it can't follow $_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT'] at runtime to find $con.

One quick fix would be to add a stub at the top of your file:

/** @var mysqli $con */

Or check your intelephense.environment.includePaths setting in VS Code and add your root path there so it can resolve the include statically.
